title: Reverse Linked List I
learningPath: Core DSA Track -> Linked List Module
learningPaths: Core DSA Track -> Linked List Module
description: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively or recursively.
inputFormat: Standard competitive programming input stream for Reverse Linked List I.
outputFormat: Standard output stream containing the computed result.
whyLearnThis: Classic pointer manipulation benchmark question required for complex list operations.
recognitionClues: Look for array/string traversal where linked list properties or sliding boundaries reduce time complexity.
hints: Maintain prev, curr, and next pointers.
Save curr.next, reverse pointer curr.next = prev, advance prev and curr.
Return prev as the new head.
approach: Iteratively reverse links using three pointers: prev initialized to null, curr to head. Continuously redirect curr.next to prev.
intuition: By maintaining optimal state or invariants during iteration, we avoid recomputing redundant subproblems.
algorithm:
1. Initialize data structures (Singly Linked List).
2. Traverse input while updating current boundary or accumulator.
3. Return result once target state is reached.
pseudocode:
prev = None, curr = head
while curr:
  next_node = curr.next
  curr.next = prev
  prev = curr
  curr = next_node
return prev
commonMistakes: Losing reference to next node before updating pointer, causing memory leaks/infinite loops.
edgeCases: Empty list (head is None), single node list.
interviewTrick: Focus on invariant preservation and spatial optimization (in-place manipulation where applicable).
revisionNotes: Key Linked List question frequently asked in FAANG/Top Tech interview loops.
